name: engineering-catalog
description: AI engineering catalog — skills, agents, workflows and bundles for GitHub Copilot and Claude Code

skills.name: ado-backlog-placement
skills.description: Find where a new task belongs on the Azure Boards backlog — check for an existing item, rank the open Features it could sit under, offer to create a Feature when none fits, then draft the PBI and create it only after an explicit yes. Optional; it asks first. Use when the user says "I need to do X" or "start working on X" with no work item id, "put this on the board", "where does this belong", or "create a PBI for …" without naming a parent.

skills.name: ado-board
skills.description: Keep the Azure Boards card in step with the code — move a work item forward (todo → doing → testing → verify → done) on evidence, and reconcile the board with pushed branches and completed pull requests. Use when the user says "move 123 to doing", "mark the bug resolved", "sync the board", "reconcile the board", "which of my items have not moved", or a session line says items have not moved. Also run `states discover` once per project before the first move.

skills.name: ado-credentials
skills.description: Preflight for Azure DevOps access — answers whether a credential is present, whether it still works against the organization, and exactly what to do if not. Run it first, then continue with the skill that needs Azure DevOps (for example qa-ado-work-item to file a bug); that skill starts only after this one answers ok. Also use when the user asks which Azure DevOps projects are connected, wants to add or remove a project (they give a board link and code links), says they now work in or want to switch to another project or team, or needs to enter or replace their PAT — on Windows all of it runs through this conversation, the user never runs a script. On macOS/Linux it proves the PAT in AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT when one is set, else the az CLI login and the azure-devops extension.

skills.name: catalog-doctor
skills.description: Runs only when asked — diagnose this engineering catalog install and repository wiring, report silent failure modes, and tell you the next fix.

skills.name: catalog-feedback
skills.description: Runs only when asked — draft and, after explicit approval, file Azure DevOps feedback about this catalog with the unit, receipt version and platform attached automatically.

skills.name: catalog-freshness
skills.description: Once per session, before other work, check whether the installed engineering catalog is outdated — run the freshness script (it is cheap, needs only git, and stays silent when nothing is due) and relay its one-line hint to the user if it prints one. Applies to every project where the catalog is installed, on Claude Code and on GitHub Copilot alike. Also use when the user asks which version of the engineering catalog is installed; then run the script with --version (-Version) and answer with the line it prints.

skills.name: grilling
skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea before any of it gets built — walk the decision tree one question at a time until there is shared understanding. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, says "grill me", asks to sharpen or pressure-test a plan, or is about to start building something whose requirements are still fuzzy.

skills.name: memory
skills.description: Project memory for every session — read the project's memory/index.md before proposing anything, load a unit file when work touches it, and write an entry only when a change is hard to reverse, not obvious without context, and the result of a real trade-off. Use when starting work in a project that has a memory folder, when about to propose an approach, and after a decision that meets the three-part test.

skills.name: memory-init
skills.description: Initialise project memory in this repository — choose the store, create the memory folder and index, point Claude and Copilot at it, install the post-commit hook, then fill the index from the code with honest evidence grades. Run once per project; safe to run again.

skills.name: project-workspace
skills.description: Search several of the team's repositories at once, read-only, and know where every repository lives on this computer. Use when the user says "find where this breaks", "search all our repositories", "which project has this code", "did this change recently", "check Warehouse, Reports and Sidecar", names more than one repository to look in, or another skill needs to look at code it does not have open. Not for one repository the user is already working in — search that one directly.

skills.name: unslop
skills.description: Cut AI tells from any writing — scan for the listed patterns, rewrite with meaning and tone kept, self-audit. Use when the user says "unslop this", "remove the AI tells", "make this sound less like AI", or when another skill hands over a text it has drafted, such as a commit message or a PR description.

skills.name: writing-great-skills
skills.description: Reference for authoring and pruning skills.

skills.name: ado-branch
skills.description: Start a task on a correctly named branch — read the Azure DevOps work item and create feature/ADO-<id>-<title>, or bug/ADO-<id>-<title> for a Bug, from main. Use when the user says "start task 12345", "create a branch for bug …", "branch for work item …", or begins work on a work item without a branch.

skills.name: ado-pr-feedback
skills.description: Address review comments on an Azure DevOps pull request — classify every comment against the current code first, fix what is valid, commit before replying, then set each thread's status (fixed / wontFix / closed) once the user approves. Use when the user says "address the PR comments", "go through the review feedback", "resolve the threads on PR 123", "CI is red on my PR", or pastes a reviewer's comment to act on.

skills.name: ado-pull-request
skills.description: Finish a task with a pull request whose title and description feed the release notes, or inspect/update Azure DevOps PR status — feat(<id>)/fix(<id>)/bug(<id>) lines written from the real diff, review offered, squash merge into main. Use when the user says "prepare the PR", "create a pull request", "the code is done", is about to push a finished branch, wants a PR dashboard/status view, or asks to update a drifted PR title/body. Not for reviewing someone else's PR, explaining what squash merge means, or working on non-Azure-DevOps PRs.

skills.name: commit
skills.description: Commit the current changes as one commit per change — split by hunk when a file carries parts of two — each with a message that follows this repository's own convention, read from its history, conventional commits when there is none, built from the diff, cleaned of AI tells, and created only after the user has reviewed which files go into which commit, read every message, and said yes. Use when the user says "commit this", "commit my changes", "write a commit message", or has finished a change and wants it recorded.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions — refuses to theorise until a tight feedback loop already goes red on this bug. Use when the user says "diagnose" or "debug this", or reports something broken, throwing, failing, flaky, or slow.

skills.name: git-sync
skills.description: Sync the current branch with base or upstream changes, merge latest main, check if behind, resolve merge conflicts, or tidy squash-merged branches. Use when the user asks to sync with remote, pull or merge upstream/main, check branch freshness or behind count, resolve git conflicts, or clean up merged branches.

skills.name: implementation-discipline
skills.description: Developer reference for implementation work — verify sub-agent diffs, re-run affected tests after base merges, think before coding, and keep a single source of truth. Use when the user asks for implementation discipline or coding principles, or when checking a sub-agent diff or what to do after merging main into a branch.

skills.name: pr-review
skills.description: Review a branch or pull request before it is opened or merged — collect the diff, launch the code-reviewer agent on a different model, and turn its findings into a short list to fix or accept. Use when the user says "review my branch", "review this PR", "check this before I open a PR", or is about to create a pull request.

skills.name: qa-ado-work-item
skills.description: Turn a tester's observation into a fact-checked Azure DevOps Bug, Task, Product Backlog Item or Feature — gather evidence from the repositories and the board first, then draft, then publish only what the user explicitly approved. Use when the user reports a defect or unexpected behaviour, asks to create or file a bug/task/PBI/feature in Azure DevOps, asks whether something is already on the board, or wants a QA observation checked against the code.

skills.name: safety-ssh
skills.description: Safe, credential-free SSH to remote servers — the assistant works only through a named connection and never sees or types passwords, usernames, hostnames, or IPs. Use this skill to actually carry out any task that lives on another machine — a server, box, host, VM, instance, prod/staging environment, build or CI agent, database server, or jump/bastion host. If fulfilling the request means logging in over SSH and doing something there — restart or bounce a service, deploy, prune docker images, dump a schema, free up disk, tail or grep remote logs, run df/du/systemctl — this is the skill, and it is the required path for doing it. Treat these as triggers: "ssh into…", "log into…", "connect to my server and…", "hop to the internal host and…", a pasted `ssh user@host`, a bare IP, or an offered SSH password/key/.env secret. Not for local-only SSH: making keys, git publickey errors, explaining ssh flags or agent forwarding, passphrases, or local rsync.

agents.name: memory-writer
agents.description: Drains the project's unrecorded-commit queue into memory entries, in isolation, so the working session spends no context on it. Use after a batch of commits, at the end of a task, or when reconcile.js reports commits memory has not caught up with.

agents.name: code-reviewer
agents.description: Independent code review of a branch or pull request on a different model than the one that wrote the code — a rubber duck that reads the diff, verifies claims against the code, and returns findings with file:line and severity. Use before opening a pull request, when asked to review a branch or PR, or when a change feels too big to trust.

agents.name: qa-triage
agents.description: Triages a tester's observation before anything is filed — separates confirmed from reported from inferred, checks the board for duplicates, and decides whether it is a bug, a backlog item, or a question. Use when a tester describes unexpected behaviour and it is not yet clear what, if anything, should be filed.

workflows.name: onboard-project
workflows.description: Guided project onboarding — preflight Azure DevOps credentials, initialise project memory, discover board states, inspect branch policies, and verify with catalog-doctor.

workflows.name: observation-to-work-item
workflows.description: From a tester's observation to an approved Azure DevOps work item — preflight the credential, triage the observation, draft, get explicit approval, publish once and read it back.

bundles.name: developers
bundles.description: Day-to-day code work with Azure DevOps and shared project memory.

bundles.name: product
bundles.description: Sharpening plans and maintaining the catalog itself.

bundles.name: qa
bundles.description: Everything a tester needs to turn observations into fact-checked work items.
